paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom served as high priest eleven years, Yoma 9a. He condemns the wealthy by example: his father left him a thousand towns and a thousand ships (see Eikhah Rabbah on “The Lord swallowed up”). Every day he slung a sack of flour over his shoulder and went from town to town and province to province to study Torah. Once his servants found him and pressed him into service. He asked to be allowed to study Torah; they said, “By the life of Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom, we will not let you go!” Never in his life did he go to inspect them; he sat studying Torah all day and night, Yoma 35b. His mother made him a tunic costing twenty thousand maneh, but his fellow priests would not let him wear it, since he appeared naked, there. (He is the mystery of the vav of the Name, the mystery of wealth and the shining of light into Malkhut. Thus ben Charsom: cheres is the sun, bestowing light on the moon, in the mystery of the charity collector distributing to the poor. Charsom has the numerical value of Shaddai: the vav of the Name bestowing on he.) Vayakhel Moshe; see Hillel. He was in Antigonus’s generation. Eikhah Rabbah, “The Lord swallowed up without pity all Jacob’s dwellings”: such as Rabbi Yishmael, Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Yeshevav, Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava, Rabbi Chutzpit, Rabbi Yehudah the baker, Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon, Rabbi Akiva, ben Azzai, and Rabbi Elazar Charsena.
